title: The Totally Rad Zone - A look at Rad Zone solo RPG
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0U0-9stDv2w

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at *Rad Zone*, Toby Lancaster's print-and-play roll-and-write solo game — a post-apocalyptic answer to anyone who has asked for something in the vein of *Four Against Darkness* or *D100 Dungeon* without the swords. He liked the review copy enough to buy the $10 PDF anyway.

You manage a bunker of ten survivors, sending one out each episode to scavenge food, water, medicine, fuel and raw materials. There are no stats and no combat rolls: characters carry a story, a trait or two and some fate dice, and gear grants narrative options rather than bonuses. Enemies must be dodged, bribed or bluffed.

Two systems carry the game. The **journey** to and from the city is a grid of icons — perils, radiation, survivors, wrecks to search — where proximity raises the odds of an encounter, and Daniel calls it a puzzle he wishes he'd invented. Inside, each isometric location map is coloured in as you **scan** for radiation with three dice, pushing your luck deeper toward better loot while the hours tick away.

His one wish is for more narrative flavour in the loot tables. Bring coloured pencils and plenty of paper — every irradiated factory needs a fresh printout.

----

Rad Zone trades combat for routing and radiation-mapping. Do solo crawls need fighting at all, or is avoiding danger the more interesting puzzle?
